title: Patch: the AI's copy of the game stops un-hiding face-down cards
thread:
**Issue #1593 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1593: Patch: the AI's copy of the game stops un-hiding face-down cards
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the practice opponent faces a question like 'choose a target' and one of the legal targets is a face-down card, a human player sees only 'Face-down card'. The computer's private copy of the game, however, can still read the real card underneath — so it can aim at the trap it is actually afraid of. The same copy keeps the full details of events it recorded mid-turn (what type a set card really is, which hand card it came from, what it targeted), even though a person in the same seat is shown none of that. Once built, the computer guesses like everyone else.

## Why

`hidden_instance_ids` removes every `Selection::Instance` in the seat's own open prompt from the hidden set (`crates/ai/src/observe.rs:225-237`), so `redact` never turns those cards into `ai:hidden` placeholders and the true `def_id` survives into every determinized world (`observe.rs:462-492`, `decide.rs:289-351`). The engine deliberately anonymizes exactly those options — a face-down card is 'the id to answer with, never the definition' (R177; `view_for.rs:1442-1462`, the invariant pinned at `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs:653-659`). Worse, the seat's own `pending.options` are kept verbatim (step 7, `observe.rs:648-654`), and a `Selection::Instance` option's label is built from `def_of(..).name` (`crates/engine/src/effects/choose.rs:150-161`) — so the option text alone names the card. Separately, `scrub_event_value` (`observe.rs:329-347`) only placeholders def-id fields on captured/queued events (trigger queue, work resumes, delayed effects, dispatch); it keeps `formerId`, `cardType`, `targets`, `answer`, `x`, `radiant` and paid costs — every field `redact_event` strips for a hidden card (`view_for.rs:1909+`, R97/R227/R448). Reachable today: any of the four plague cards or a backrow-scoped target prompt puts enemy face-down cards into the AI's own options.

## Proposal

In `crates/ai/src/observe.rs`: only un-hide a prompt-offered instance when the seat may actually read that card (reuse the view's readability predicates — `is_face_down_to`/`announced_face_down_to`/`backrow_is_public`, already imported); for options that still point at hidden cards, overwrite `label` with the same 'Face-down card' wording the player's view shows; and extend `scrub_event_value` with the field-level cases `redact_event` applies (drop `formerId`/`x`/`answer`/`embiggened`, force `cardType` to `"Trap"` and `targets` to sentinels on a face-down announce, sentinel `position` on `shuffledIn`, drop `radiant`/`cost` on hidden cards).

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/observe.rs`; the mirror contract lives in `crates/engine/src/view_for.rs` and the engine's own invariant at `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs:653-659`. Spec §9.9, §10.8, §10.10; rulings R97, R177, R227, R448, R762.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test builds a state where the AI seat holds a prompt offering an enemy face-down backrow card; after `redact`, that instance's `def_id` is `ai:hidden` and the option's label is the face-down wording — both fail today.
- [ ] A test puts a hidden card's `cardAnnounced`/`cardPlayed`/`cardResolved` into a queued/captured resume; after `redact`, `formerId`, `cardType`, `targets`, `answer`, `x` and `costPaid` are absent or placeholdered exactly as the view strips them.
- [ ] Readable options (the seat's own cards, revealed cards) still un-hide as before — no over-scrubbing.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` green; `cargo jackioh gate` smoke stays green.

## Size and risks

Medium, confined to `crates/ai` (pure). The main risk is over-scrubbing — hiding information the seat legitimately has (a card it revealed itself); the fix must reuse the view's readability predicates, not a blanket ban. Determinization keeps respecting shown costs (R762), so sampling quality is unchanged.
```
